title: The setup wizard remembers saved rows by spreadsheet row number and keeps them when the CSV is replaced or edited, so rows of a second or corrected file are skipped as "Already saved by this setup" and never written
steps: 1. Demo, open /aircraft/setup/demo-206?step=inspections. 2. Paste an inspections CSV with two rows (Hunt annual, Hunt 100-hour), go to Save, click 'Save 2 inspections and 0 ADs', wait for 'Setup saved for N206MA'. Do not click 'forget this draft' (e.g. follow the Inspections link, as the notice asks first). 3. Return to the Inspections step (stepper or Setup chip) and replace the text with a different file of two more inspections (Hunt ELT battery, Hunt pitot-static). 4. Open Review, then Save. The same happens after a half-way failure when 'Fix the file' is used to delete or insert a row above unsaved rows: every later row inherits a saved row's number.
expected: The two new inspections are planned and saved; only rows that really are on the aircraft are skipped (the name check already does that).
actual: Review shows Inspections: To save 0, Skipped 2; the collapsed 'Skipped rows (2)' reads 'Hunt ELT battery: Already saved by this setup' and 'Hunt pitot-static: Already saved by this setup'; the Save step says 'Nothing to save'. Neither inspection exists on the aircraft. The same applies to the AD file ('ad:<row>' keys). The administrator is told the rows are saved when they are not, so inspection schedules or AD compliance are silently missing from the aircraft.
evidence: shots/newa-na1-review.png; output of the repro; src/domain/aircraftSetup.ts:488 and :646 (key = `inspection:${r.row}` / `ad:${r.row}`), :495-496 (done wins over the on-record check); src/components/AircraftSetup.tsx:578-584 (update() keeps `done` when inspectionCsv/adCsv change; only clear() resets it)
suspect: src/components/AircraftSetup.tsx:578 (done not reset or re-keyed when the CSV text changes) and src/domain/aircraftSetup.ts:488 (row-number keys)
notes: docs/aircraft-setup.md promises 'a second run cannot duplicate them' via the name/AD-number check, which is sufficient on its own; the positional `done` list adds the false skip. Key the saved rows by normalized name / AD number (or by request id), or clear `done` for a file when its text changes. The draft persists in localStorage until sign-out, so the stale keys survive days.

title: The paper check dates and groups flights by the UTC date of their start, not the pilot's local date, so evening flights (west of UTC) or morning flights (east of UTC) get the wrong day and month-end flights land in the wrong month's check and totals
steps: 1. Browser time zone America/Chicago; demo. 2. Flight log > Log a completed flight, N206MA, Flight date & time 2026-10-31 23:30, save. The flight log shows 'Oct 31, 2026 · 23:30'. 3. Paper check (month) > Month 2026-10 > Save CSV; then Month 2026-11 > Save CSV.
expected: docs/reconciliation.md: 'every flight that started in the month by the pilot's local date'. October lists the flight dated 2026-10-31 and counts its 0.4 h; November does not.
actual: October's CSV has only the Totals row (0 flights, 0.0 h). November's has "Flight","2026-11-01",... and counts it in November's totals. More generally the Date column is the UTC date: in US Central every flight after 18:00 (19:00 in summer) prints the next day; in UTC+3 every flight before 03:00, in UTC+10 every flight before 10:00 prints the previous day, so the monthly comparison with the paper logbook shows false mismatches. The PDF uses the same rows.
evidence: Output of the repro; src/domain/reconciliation.ts:283-287 (inMonth = startsWith on the ISO string, comment claims the string is in the writer's zone) and :291 (date: f.startTime.slice(0, 10)); src/components/FlightForm.tsx:792 (startTime: new Date(...).toISOString(), always UTC 'Z') and GuidedFlight.tsx:1095/1325 (same); src/domain/reconciliation.test.ts:109-112 pins the promise with a '-07:00' offset string that the app never writes, so the test cannot catch this.
notes: The flight's start is stored as a UTC instant with no zone, so 'the pilot's local date' can only be approximated with the viewer's zone (localDate(Date.parse(startTime))) unless the flight stores its local date. The records package flights.csv prints the raw UTC ISO string in 'Date and time' (unlabelled column, value ends in Z) - same root, less misleading. Also a test-gap: fix the fixture to use Z strings.

title: A records package built offline carries only the device's recent change-log entries, but README.txt and change-log.csv do not say so; the README still states that the change log lists every change
steps: 1. Demo (or any signed-in device), open View aircraft for N206MA and export one records package while online (this caches the PDF library). 2. Go offline. 3. Export records package again and open README.txt and change-log.csv from the ZIP.
expected: docs/records-export.md: 'offline, only the recent entries on the device are included and the README says so.' README.txt (the file an inspector reads first) and ideally change-log.csv state that the change log is partial.
actual: README.txt is identical to an online package: 'change-log.csv - Change log (N rows).' and 'Corrections are appended ... so the change log lists every change.' Nothing says the log is partial. change-log.csv has no marker either (with no device entries it reads "No changes recorded"). Only a note under the Change log table inside records.pdf mentions it. An inspector or buyer working from the CSV/README takes a partial change log as complete.
evidence: Output of the repro (README printed); src/domain/recordsPackage.ts:227-262 (recordsReadme takes no completeness input; section notes are not written to the README), :770-774 (the only place the partial note exists, PDF notes); src/data/recordsPackage.ts:166-171; docs/records-export.md line 31
notes: Same gap when the 400-page cap (MAX_CHANGE_LOG_PAGES) cuts the log while online: complete=false, and the PDF note then wrongly says 'only the recent changes available on this device. Reconnect and export again' (src/data/recordsPackage.ts:186). Consider refusing or clearly labelling an offline package, since it is what an FAA inspector receives.

title: A second logbook photo with the same file name taken for the same unsynced flight silently replaces the first on the device (iOS names every camera capture image.jpg), while the notice says the photo was saved
steps: 1. Demo, Flight log > Log a completed flight on N206MA; go offline before Save flight. 2. In the 'Flight saved' prompt add a photo named image.jpg (photo of the first logbook line). 3. Add a second, different photo also named image.jpg (the second line or the facing page). 4. Open the Sync center, reconnect, open the flight in the Flight log.
expected: Both photos are kept on the device and uploaded (as happens online, where two uploads of the same name are both stored), or the second is refused with a message.
actual: Each add shows 'Photo saved on this device. It will upload once the record has synced.', but the prompt shows one 'waiting' thumbnail, the Sync center one 'Photo waiting' row, and after sync the flight has one photo: the first capture is gone without warning.
evidence: Output of the repro; src/data/logbookPhotos.ts:36-46 (pendingPhotoKey = `<linkedUuid>:<name>`, 'choosing the same file again replaces the queued copy'); src/data/store.ts:437-445 and :556-560
notes: The replacement is deliberate for 'the same file chosen twice', but file name is not identity: iOS Safari/Chrome give every camera capture the name image.jpg, and the control opens the rear camera on a phone (docs/logbook-photos.md). Key by a generated id (or name+size+lastModified hash) instead. Mechanism proven in Chromium with two different files named image.jpg; the iOS naming is from platform behaviour, not tested on a device.

title: The AD setup template accepts any text as ad_number, so an AD number that Excel has rewritten as a date (2011-10-09 saved as 10/9/2011) is planned and saved as the AD's number with no error or warning
steps: 1. Download the AD compliance CSV template from the wizard, open it in Excel, type AD 2011-10-09 in ad_number (Excel converts date-shaped text to a date) and save as CSV: the cell is written as 10/9/2011. 2. Upload or paste the file in step 4 (e.g. row `10/9/2011,Seat rail,yes,,,,,,no,`). 3. Open Review and Save.
expected: The row is refused ("Row 2: AD number must look like 2011-10-09") or at least listed under Check, as the same file's date columns are (they refuse anything but YYYY-MM-DD).
actual: parseAdSetupCsv accepts it and planAircraftSetup plans 'AD 10/9/2011' with no error or warning; the commit saves an airworthiness record numbered 10/9/2011, reviewed (not Needs review). The duplicate check (adNumber) does not match it to 2011-10-09, so a later FAA search import adds the same AD again as Needs review. AD numbers are date-shaped (YYYY-NN-NN), so this is the normal outcome of preparing the file in a spreadsheet.
evidence: vitest output of the repro (planned: ['10/9/2011'], flagged: false); src/domain/aircraftSetup.ts:233 (number: z.string().trim().min(1).max(100)), :287-299, :646-668; also '=2024-05-01' is accepted (H/work-newa explore output)
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-ad-number.test.ts (copy to src/domain/, run `npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-newa-ad-number.test.ts`; it fails today)
notes: The Airworthiness form has no AD-number format rule either (adSourceSchema), so a strict pattern is an owner decision; a Check warning for numbers that do not match /^\d{2,4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(R\d+)?$/ would be enough for the wizard. Related, same cause: Excel also rewrites the template's ISO dates to M/D/YYYY, which the wizard refuses with only 'Row 2: Invalid ISO date' (no hint of the YYYY-MM-DD format or that a spreadsheet changed it); docs/aircraft-setup.md does not warn about spreadsheets reformatting either column.

title: The setup wizard decodes every uploaded CSV as UTF-8, so a file saved by Excel as plain "CSV (Comma delimited)" (Windows-1252) has its non-ASCII characters replaced by U+FFFD and planned for saving with no error or warning
steps: 1. Demo, /aircraft/setup/demo-206?step=inspections. 2. Upload a Windows-1252 CSV whose row is `Inspección anual,,12,,,2026-03-15,,,,§91.409 – 12 mo` (what Excel's default CSV format writes). 3. Read the parsed table, then open Review.
expected: The upload is refused or flagged (invalid UTF-8 / replacement characters found: 'Save the file as CSV UTF-8'), since docs/aircraft-setup.md requires UTF-8.
actual: The table shows 'Inspecci�n anual' and '�91.409 � 12 mo'; no alert; the review plans 1 inspection to save, so the corrupted name and manual reference are written to the inspection record and its change-log entry.
evidence: Output of the repro; src/components/AircraftSetupHistory.tsx:688-700 (readCsvFile: onCsv(await file.text()))
notes: Decode with new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal:true}) and refuse on failure, or warn when the text contains U+FFFD. The same file.text() pattern may exist in the other CSV imports (component templates, job cards); not checked here. A UTF-16 file with a BOM decodes correctly in Chromium.

title: Logbook page photos share the aircraft's 200-current-document cap with Form 337 copies, so after 200 flight photos the server refuses every further photo and every Form 337 upload on that aircraft
steps: 1. On one aircraft, pilots attach a logbook line photo to each flight (the prompt after every saved flight asks for one) until 200 are current. 2. A mechanic uploads a Form 337 copy to that aircraft (or a pilot adds photo 201).
expected: A permanent 14 CFR 91.417(a)(2)(vi) status record can still be filed; routine reconciliation photos do not consume the allowance for it (separate caps per category, or a cap sized for one photo per flight).
actual: ConvexError 'This aircraft already has the maximum of 200 current documents.' for the Form 337 copy and for every new photo; photos queued offline turn into 'Needs attention' in the Sync center. The only way out is archiving photos one at a time with a reason, which removes them from their flights and from the paper check's Photo column. At one or two flights a day the cap is reached in three to six months; the cap was sized for Form 337 copies ('Status records accumulate over an aircraft's life').
evidence: vitest output of the repro (rejected with the cap message); convex/aircraftFiles.ts:131 and :299-309 (countCurrentFiles counts every category); src/domain/aircraftFiles.ts:79-83; docs/logbook-photos.md 'Photos count toward the aircraft's limit of 200 current documents'
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-photo-cap.test.ts (copy to convex/, run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-newa-photo-cap.test.ts`; it fails today)
notes: Documented behaviour, so the limit itself is the owner's call; reported because any user with flight permission can (innocently) block Form 337 filing, and the feature's own usage pattern exhausts the cap within months. The snapshot also loads every aircraft file with a storage URL for every reader (aircraftFileList), which grows with one row per flight.

title: The records package leaves out the aircraft's logbook page photos (signed-page photos of work orders and flight-line photos): they are neither copied into the ZIP nor listed in any table or the README
steps: 1. Attach a signed page photo to a completed work order (or a line photo to a flight) on an aircraft. 2. Export records package for that aircraft. 3. Look for the photo in the ZIP, the CSVs, records.pdf and README.txt.
expected: docs/records-export.md calls the package 'the complete record set Angel One holds for one aircraft'. The photos stored on the aircraft record (aircraftFiles, category logbook-page) are in the package, or README.txt says they are not included.
actual: buildRecordsPackage takes only category 'form-337' files and work-order attachments. A logbook-page file appears nowhere: not under files/, not in work-orders.csv or flights.csv (no photo column), not in README.txt's FILES or SKIPPED FILES. A buyer or inspector receives no sign that photos of the signed pages exist.
evidence: vitest output of the repro; src/domain/recordsPackage.ts:171 (files: form337Files + attachmentFiles), :694-696 (category === 'form-337'); browser export in H/work-newa/pkg1 (README lists no photo folder)
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-package-photos.test.ts (copy to src/domain/, run `npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-newa-package-photos.test.ts`; it fails today)
notes: Both features landed on 9 Nov, so this may simply be unplanned. If photos are deliberately excluded, the README and docs should say so. Archived photos would follow the Form 337 pattern (an archived/ folder).

title: Offline, on a device that has not built a PDF before, Export records package and the paper check (Save CSV included) fail with the browser's raw error "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://…/assets/recordsPackage-….js"
steps: 1. Open the app (service worker installed and controlling the page), without having exported any PDF on this device. 2. Go offline. 3. View aircraft > Export records package. 4. Flight log > Paper check (month) > Save CSV.
expected: A message a user can act on ('Connect once to download the export tools'), or the export works; the CSV paper check needs no PDF library at all. docs/records-export.md describes an offline package without this precondition.
actual: Both show role=alert text 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://127.0.0.1:4400/assets/recordsPackage-Cd9qdOVP.js' (and paperCheckReport-….js). No file is saved. The chunks are precached, but they statically import jsPDF, which vite.config.ts leaves out of the precache and src/sw.ts caches only after first use online.
evidence: Output of the repro; vite.config.ts:112-118 (globIgnores assets/jspdf*.js, fonts/*.ttf); src/sw.ts:57-66; src/components/ExportRecordsPackage.tsx:47-58 and PaperCheck.tsx:138-150 (errorText(e, fallback) shows the raw message); src/data/paperCheckReport.ts:13 (jsPDF imported at module top, also for the CSV path)
notes: After one online PDF export on the device both work offline (that is how NA-3 was reproduced). Other lazy PDF exports probably show the same raw text; not checked.

title: An overdue or due-soon inspection saved without a Reference (the setup template's optional manual_reference) grounds the aircraft with a blank reason: the Dashboard card, the aircraft's Status notes and the "is grounded" alert read just "overdue"
steps: 1. Set up an aircraft in the wizard and load an inspections CSV with manual_reference left blank, one row overdue: `Transponder,,24,,,2024-10-15,,,,`. Save. 2. Open the Dashboard, View aircraft, and Alerts.
expected: The reason names the inspection, as every other screen does with `reference || description`: 'Transponder overdue'.
actual: Dashboard card: 'N734HT Grounded ... overdue' (nothing before 'overdue'); aircraft detail 'STATUS NOTES overdue'; Alerts: 'N734HT is grounded' with the text 'overdue'. With a reference the same places read '91.413 overdue'. The grounding reason of an aircraft does not say which inspection is overdue.
evidence: shots/newa-na11-blank-reference.png (aircraft detail); browser output in notes; vitest output of the repro; src/domain/aircraftStatus.ts:193-199 (`${reference} overdue`, `${reference} due soon`) versus alerts.ts:275, statusSheet.ts:254, Dashboard.tsx:767 which fall back to the description
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-blank-reference.test.ts (copy to src/domain/, run `npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-newa-blank-reference.test.ts`; it fails today)
notes: Not specific to the wizard (the Inspections form marks Reference 'Optional' too), but the wizard makes it the common case: its docs say blank cells mean unknown and manual_reference is the last, optional-looking column. The same label feeds urgent grounding alerts (email/push); not checked there.

title: Two setup runs on one aircraft from snapshots that do not yet show each other's rows (two administrators, two tabs or devices) save every inspection twice: the server has no duplicate check for inspection schedules, only for ADs
steps: 1. Two administrators (or one in two tabs) open Set up an aircraft for the same aircraft with the same inspections file (Annual, 100-hour) and each reach the Save step. 2. Both click Save. In the demo: tab 1 at the Save step, tab 2 commits 'Annual', then tab 1 commits.
expected: docs/aircraft-setup.md: 'the review still skips rows whose inspection name or AD number is already on the aircraft, so a second run cannot duplicate them.' The second commit's inspections are refused like its ADs ('This AD already exists for the selected asset.').
actual: Each inspection.save is accepted: the aircraft holds Annual, 100-hour, Annual, 100-hour (demo two-tab run: 'Annual' twice; convex-test: 4 inspections, 7 audit rows). Duplicate schedules then each need completing; completing one leaves its twin running to overdue and grounding the aircraft. The run's plan is fixed when Save is clicked (run.actions), so rows saved by someone else during a long commit are not re-checked either.
evidence: vitest output of the repro (inspections: 4); demo two-tab run output in H/work-newa (wiz4.cjs: STATE insp [Annual, Annual, 100-hour]); src/domain/aircraftSetup.ts:481-507 (client-side `existing` set only); src/domain/management/inspections.ts:31-55 (no duplicate rule) versus src/domain/airworthiness.ts:786-794
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-wizard-duplicates.test.ts (copy to convex/, run `npx vitest run convex/zz-hunt-newa-wizard-duplicates.test.ts`; it fails today)
suspect: src/domain/management/inspections.ts:31 (saveInspection has no same-name guard for new records)
notes: Held in the same test: wizard writes go through management.execute / airworthiness.save, one audit row each (inspection.save with the setup reason; ad.save with no reason text), a retry with the same request ids writes nothing, a pilot is refused. A server-side duplicate rule for inspections changes the ordinary Inspections form too, hence owner decision; a cheaper fix is for the commit loop to re-check each row against the live snapshot just before sending.

title: For an aircraft whose total time is its meter plus an adjustment, the Inspections screen prints the due total time with the unit "h Hobbs" (or Tach), so the figure reads as a meter reading that is off by the adjustment
steps: 1. Set up an aircraft with Current Hobbs 2300.0, Total time adjustment 37.2 (total 2,337.2 h; a replaced Hobbs meter), source Hobbs. 2. Load an inspection `100-hour,100,,,,2026-08-14,2290.0,,,91.409(b)` and save (last done at 2,290.0 h total time, as the template asks). 3. Open Inspections.
expected: The due point is labelled as total time ('Due 2,390.0 h total time'), or shown as the meter reading it corresponds to (Hobbs 2,352.8).
actual: The row reads 'Due 2,390.0 h Hobbs · 52.8 h remaining'. 2,390.0 is aircraft total time (Hobbs + 37.2); the Hobbs meter reads 2,352.8 at that point. A pilot or mechanic who flies to 'Hobbs 2,390' overflies the inspection by the adjustment. The remaining figure is right. In the demo every aircraft has adjustment 0.0, so the label never looked wrong there; real aircraft loaded this week will mostly have an adjustment.
evidence: shots/newa-na12-hobbs-label.png; output of the repro; src/components/Management.tsx:714-717 (due: hours(i.dueSeconds), basis: hourBasis) and :733-737 (hourBasis returns aircraftMeterLabels[a.meter])
notes: The stored values are correct (dueSeconds is total time, checked by hand: 2,290.0 + 100 = 2,390.0; total 2,337.2; remaining 52.8). Only the label is wrong. The Dashboard card shows TOTAL and HOBBS separately and gets it right. Other places that print a due-hours figure beside a meter name were not all checked (owner portal 'Total time (Hobbs)' is honest).

title: Sibling of NA-1: a component template CSV without the optional ID column gets positional row ids, and "already applied to this aircraft" is keyed on that id, so a row inserted above existing rows is silently skipped when the edited template is applied again
steps: 1. Components > New template / import CSV with the four required columns only (Component type, ATA chapter, Part number, Component Name): Engine, Propeller. Apply it to an aircraft. 2. Later add 'Left magneto' as the first row of the spreadsheet and import the file into the same template (Edit template > Import component CSV), save. 3. Apply the template to the same aircraft, selecting the new row.
expected: Left magneto is added as a Setup incomplete entry; only rows that were really applied are skipped (docs/component-templates.md: 'Reapplying the same template rows to the same aircraft does not create duplicates').
actual: applyComponentTemplate returns no additions and no error: the magneto now has row id '1', which the aircraft's Engine setup already holds, so it is treated as applied. The component is never recommended for that aircraft.
evidence: vitest output of the repro (expected ['Left magneto'], received []); src/domain/componentTemplates.ts:360 (id: get('ID') || String(index + 1)), :288-290 and :391-402 (mapAppliedSetups keyed by row.id)
repro: repro/newa/zz-hunt-newa-template-row-ids.test.ts (copy to src/domain/, run `npx vitest run src/domain/zz-hunt-newa-template-row-ids.test.ts`; it fails today)
notes: Proven in the domain function the server and demo both run; the browser path (file import into an existing template, then the wizard's 'Apply template') was not driven. Editing in the text box is safer because the editor regenerates the CSV with the ID column filled. Other importers checked for the same pattern: maintenance CSV import keys on the file's own required `id` column per manual (documented: 'Use the same IDs on subsequent exports'); the wizard's localStorage `done` list (NA-1) is the only client-side saved-rows list (grep of localStorage use). Task-file and logbook imports were not examined.

title: The server sends aircraft owners every current logbook page photo of their aircraft (storage URL, file name, linked flight or work-order id), although the owner view is whitelisted to hold no flights and only Form 337 copies
steps: 1. A pilot attaches a logbook line photo to a flight (or a mechanic a signed page photo to a work order) on an aircraft that has an Aircraft owners group. 2. A user who is only in the owner group loads the app (api.operations.snapshot) and inspects the snapshot (devtools, or the 7-day offline copy in IndexedDB).
expected: As the code comment at src/domain/ownerView.ts:90 says: 'Form 337 copies are status records kept for the owner; owners see only current, not archived, copies.' The owner snapshot has flights: [] and stripped work orders, so it carries no photos of flight log lines or signed pages.
actual: snapshot.aircraftFiles holds both 'form-337:337-2019.pdf' and 'logbook-page:flight-line.jpg', each with a working storage URL and the linked flight uuid. The owner portal screen filters by category so nothing shows, but the data and file links are delivered to the owner's device.
evidence: vitest output of the repro; src/domain/ownerView.ts:90-94 (filter on aircraft and current only, written before the logbook-page category existed); convex/operations.ts:122-124; docs/records-export.md 'Aircraft owners keep the status sheet PDF only: the package holds flights, work detail and the change log, which the owner portal leaves out'

Impact is limited (photos of the owner's own aircraft's logbook), but a flight line shows pilot names and routes that the owner view otherwise withholds. Held in the same probe: api.auditHistory.page refuses an owner ('Aircraft owner access is read-only.') and a board member (existing boardView test); the board snapshot carries no files.

title: An aircraft that the setup wizard has only created (no inspections, no components, ADs not reviewed) is labelled "Airworthy" on the Aircraft page and the Dashboard while its history is still being loaded
steps: 1. Aircraft > Set up an aircraft, fill step 1 and click Add aircraft. 2. Without loading inspections or ADs, open Aircraft and the Dashboard (as a pilot would during the days the administrator is still loading history).
expected: A status that does not assert airworthiness for an aircraft with setup gaps, e.g. 'Setup incomplete' or 'Unknown', as the aircraft dialog itself says 'Missing information never implies aircraft readiness'.
actual: Aircraft page: 'N15NEW ... 2,300.0 h Airworthy ... Components missing, Inspections missing, ADs not reviewed'. Dashboard card: 'N15NEW Airworthy ... No inspection schedule · Maintenance information needed', with Log flight offered. The computed level is 'airworthy' whenever no loaded record is due, so an aircraft with an overdue annual that has not been typed in yet reads Airworthy until the row is saved (and each partially loaded step in between).
evidence: shots/newa-na15-empty-airworthy.png; output of the repro; src/domain/aircraftStatus.ts:46-50 and :67-87 (no findings means level airworthy); src/domain/aircraftSetup.ts:367-392 (setupStatus knows the gaps but only feeds the chips)
notes: The label predates the wizard (GLOSSARY: computed level), so changing it is the owner's decision; reported because the wizard now creates aircraft before their records exist and this week's loading will leave real aircraft in that state for hours or days. A cheap mitigation is for the wizard to create the aircraft with profile status Grounded/Maintenance until setup is complete, or to show the chip text in place of 'Airworthy' while setupStatus().gaps is non-empty.

title: Leaving the wizard's Save step while a commit is running and returning shows the Save button again; clicking it starts a second commit over the rows the first has not reached, so those inspections are saved twice
steps: 1. Demo, /aircraft/setup/demo-206?step=inspections, paste a 300-row inspections file. 2. Open Save and click 'Save 300 inspections and 0 ADs'. 3. While the list is still working, click 'Review (dry run)' in the stepper, then 'Save' again. 4. The step shows 'Save 293 inspections and 0 ADs' with no sign that a save is running; click it. 5. Wait for 'Setup saved', then count the aircraft's inspections.
expected: One commit per aircraft at a time: on return the step shows the running commit's progress (or the button stays disabled), and no row is written twice ('a second run cannot duplicate them', docs/aircraft-setup.md).
actual: Both loops run to the end. 507 inspections exist for 300 rows; 207 are saved twice, each with its own change-log entry. The second plan has new record uuids and request ids, so request-id idempotency does not help, and the server has no duplicate rule for inspections (NA-11). For AD rows the second loop instead stops on 'This AD already exists for the selected asset.' On the real server a row takes a network round trip, so even a 30-row file leaves seconds to do this.
evidence: Output of the repro ('inspections saved: 507 for 300 rows; saved twice: 207'); src/components/AircraftSetupHistory.tsx:183 (run state lives in CommitStep and is lost on unmount), :188-192 and :289-314 (commitActions is not cancelled on unmount and nothing records that it is running); src/components/AircraftSetup.tsx:242 (CommitStep remounts per visit)
notes: Same root as NA-16. Keep the run in the wizard (or the store) rather than in the step, block a second start while one is running, and re-check each row against the live snapshot before sending. Cleaning up means archiving every duplicate schedule by hand.

title: While a wizard commit is running, the other steps show no sign of it, and every row it saves writes the old CSV text back over whatever is typed in the Inspections or AD step
steps: 1. Demo, /aircraft/setup/demo-206?step=inspections, paste a 400-row inspections file, open Save and click Save. 2. While it runs, click the Inspections step and add a row at the end of the text.
expected: Either the CSV steps are read-only with a 'saving' notice while a commit runs, or the edit is kept.
actual: The Inspections step looks idle (no progress or notice). The added row disappears from the text box within about a second, and the stored draft has the old text again: each `drafts.update({done})` from the loop spreads the draft object captured when Save was clicked.

title: The "mechanic and administrator only" rule for the records package exists only as a hidden button: a pilot or read-only member receives the same data (snapshot records and the aircraft's full change log by paging) from the server
steps: 1. Sign in as a user with read + flight on an aircraft (no maintenance). 2. Call api.operations.snapshot and api.auditHistory.page({aircraftUuid, cursor: null, numItems: 100}).
expected: If the package is meant to be restricted (docs/records-export.md 'Who can export: users with maintenance permission, Flight Program administrators and system administrators'), the change-log paging for an aircraft refuses others.
actual: The pilot's snapshot holds the aircraft's work orders, discrepancies, files and flights, and auditHistory.page returns the aircraft's entries ('OK ... isDone: true'). Owners and board members are refused ('Aircraft owner access is read-only.'; board covered by convex/boardView.test.ts). The docs do say the server scopes only what each user can already see, so this is consistent with the design; it is recorded because the task brief expected a server refusal for pilots.
evidence: convex-test probe output kept in notes/newa.md (owner refused, pilot OK); src/components/ExportRecordsPackage.tsx:41 (client-side `can(..., 'maintenance')` only); convex/auditHistory.ts:84-104
notes: No change needed if 'who can export' is a convenience rule. If it is a confidentiality rule, it has to be enforced where the data is served.

title: aircraftFiles.upload trusts the declared name and MIME type: SVG bytes named x.png, HTML named x.pdf and HEIC bytes named IMG.jpg are stored as logbook page photos
steps: 1. As a user with flight permission call api.aircraftFiles.upload for a flight photo with name 'x.png', type 'image/png' and SVG text as bytes (or name 'IMG_1.jpg', type 'image/jpeg' and HEIC bytes).
expected: The server checks the first bytes against the declared type (JPEG FF D8, PNG 89 50 4E 47, RIFF/WEBP, %PDF) and refuses a mismatch, so the HEIC refusal cannot be bypassed by a rename and every stored photo can be shown.
actual: All three are accepted and stored with the declared type; the audit row records the declared type. A renamed HEIC then shows as a broken thumbnail on the flight. Size limits hold (0 bytes and 7 MiB + 1 refused, 7 MiB accepted), 'image/svg+xml' and upper-case 'IMAGE/JPEG' are refused, another program's programUuid is refused.
evidence: convex-test probe output in notes/newa.md; convex/aircraftFiles.ts:181-199; src/domain/inventoryAttachments.ts:50-63 (name and type only)
notes: Same class as the known T2 (upload link accepts any bytes), on the action-bytes path that all attachments share; not exploitable for script execution because the blob is served with the declared image/PDF type. Recorded as Info so the fix for T2 covers this path too.
